questions.prompt: What is the formula of magnesium oxide? (Mg²⁺, O²⁻)
questions.explain: Crossing gives Mg₂O₂; simplify by dividing by 2.

questions.prompt: What is the formula of sodium sulfate? (Na⁺, SO₄²⁻)
What is the formula of aluminium sulfate? (Al³⁺, SO₄²⁻)
questions.explain: 2 × (+3) = +6 and 3 × (−2) = −6. Brackets for more than one sulfate.

questions.prompt: What is the formula of ammonium chloride? (NH₄⁺, Cl⁻)
questions.explain: Both have valency 1, so they combine 1 : 1.

questions.prompt: Match each compound to its formula.
questions.explain: Work each out from the ion charges.

questions.prompt: Why does calcium hydroxide need brackets, Ca(OH)₂, but calcium chloride doesn’t?
options: Brackets show it is a liquid
OH is a group of atoms that must be doubled together
questions.explain: Without brackets, CaOH₂ would mean 1 O and 2 H.

questions.prompt: A compound contains Fe³⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. What is its formula?
A student writes the formula of aluminium oxide as AlO. Explain the mistake and show how to get the correct formula.
questions.modelAnswer: Aluminium ions are Al³⁺ and oxide ions are O²⁻. In AlO the charges would be +3 and −2, which don’t cancel. Criss-crossing the valencies gives Al₂O₃: 2 × (+3) = +6 and 3 × (−2) = −6, a total of zero, so the compound is neutral.
rubric: Derives Al₂O₃ with a charge check
